subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Should an authorized security or dependency reviewer approve the exact current `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency update and nonce-payload ownership model for the exec-approvals authorization sidecar?
rationale: The patch is intentionally fail-closed and its mechanical behavior is covered, but accepting a dependency-backed ownership rule at an authorization boundary is a maintainer security decision rather than a contributor-side repair choice.

options.title: Approve after exact-head proof
options.body: Authorize the dependency graph after reviewing the shared lock contract and fresh current-head FUSE output for both lock paths.

options.title: Keep the previous release rule
options.body: Reject the ownership-rule change and retain the inode-based release behavior, accepting continued filesystem-identity drift failures.

options.title: Split the dependency decision
options.body: Require a maintainer-owned package review first, then revisit the OpenClaw consumer patch against the approved release.

recommendation.title: Approve after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Authorize the dependency graph after reviewing the shared lock contract and fresh current-head FUSE output for both lock paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the active production reproduction and maintain the related async-path analysis, making them the strongest technical routing contact; authorization remains a reviewer decision.
